text: `curl http://localhost:8080/` gives connection refused, but `sudo service myapp status` (or `pgrep -f myapp-server`) shows the process is up. So it's alive, just not on 8080. Find out what it's actually bound to: `sudo ss -tlnp`.

`ss -tlnp` shows the python process listening on `:9091`, not `:8080`. Odd -- check its config or command line for a hardcoded port first: `cat /proc/$(pgrep -f myapp-server)/cmdline`. There isn't one. This app resolves its port a different way.

Read `/usr/local/bin/myapp-server.py`: it calls `socket.getservbyname("myapp", "tcp")` instead of using a literal port number -- it looks its own port up from the system-wide service-name database, `/etc/services`. Check that file: `grep myapp /etc/services`.

`/etc/services` still has `myapp 9091/tcp` -- left over from before the app's port was reassigned to 8080, and never updated when the migration happened. Fix the entry (`/etc/services` isn't a bind-mounted file, so `sudo sed -i 's/9091/8080/' /etc/services` works fine here), then restart the app so it re-resolves the port: `sudo service myapp restart`. Re-test `curl http://localhost:8080/`.
